claims.text: The initial AlCoCrFeNi eutectic high-entropy alloy has a dual-phase lamellar structure.
The initial alloy exhibits catastrophic interfacial cracking and low room-temperature ductility because of stress concentration at phase interfaces.

Room-temperature severe plastic deformation followed by a short anneal will transform the lamellar AlCoCrFeNi microstructure into a patterned configuration containing coherent nanotwins and ultrafine grains.
Room-temperature high-pressure torsion produces twinning in CoCrFeMnNi.
Severe plastic deformation of AlCoCrFeNi will generate extreme grain refinement and a high defect density.
GPa-range pressure or high strain rate at 293 K will induce deformation twinning rather than only dislocation slip in AlCoCrFeNi.
An anneal at approximately 900 °C for 3 minutes is an appropriate post-deformation treatment window.
A short 900 °C anneal will stabilize coherent nanotwins in AlCoCrFeNi without appreciable grain coarsening.
Annealing temperatures at or above 900 °C are consistent with FCC-phase stability in the target alloy.
Keeping the anneal short will prevent sigma-phase precipitation in AlCoCrFeNi.
Coherent nanotwin boundaries and ultrafine grains impede dislocation pile-up while still allowing dislocation transmission.
The patterned nanotwin and ultrafine-grain structure will replace the brittle lamellar interfaces.
A dislocation approaching a coherent twin boundary can dissociate, with one partial crossing onto a conjugate slip system and the other remaining mobile along the boundary.
Dislocation interactions with coherent twin boundaries will promote strain hardening and suppress interface-scale stress concentration in AlCoCrFeNi.
The proposed treatment will arrest catastrophic interfacial cracking and promote uniform room-temperature plasticity.
The treatment will significantly increase room-temperature elongation and fracture toughness without a proportional reduction in yield strength.
Exceeding the applicable annealing stability limit or annealing too long will cause sigma-phase formation and degrade ductility.
Extreme shear strain, rather than hydrostatic pressure and heating alone, is necessary to produce the patterned twin structure and associated ductility enhancement.
